description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage of different models as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot includes six lines representing different models: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with square markers), and ROME (green line with cross markers). The Base model starts at approximately 65% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends around 70% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEND model starts at around 70% and ends near 80%. The FT model begins at about 65% and ends close to 75%. The MEMIT model starts at approximately 70% and ends around 78%. The IKE model begins at around 68% and ends near 76%. The ROME model starts at about 72% and ends close to 80%. All lines show a general upward trend, indicating an increase in accuracy with the number of co-occurrences.
